Step 1: 1100 is a common year (not divisible by 400, but divisible by 100, so not a leap year).  
Step 2: 140 days before Feb 24, 1100.  
Go back 24 days → Jan 31, 1100.  
Remaining days: 140 − 24 = 116 days earlier.  
Step 3: 116 days before Jan 31, 1100:  
Back 31 days → Dec 31, 1100? No, that’s forward; we go backward into previous year.  
Actually: Jan 31 back 31 days → Jan 1, 1100.  
Remaining: 116 − 31 = 85 days before Jan 1, 1100.  
Step 4: 85 days before Jan 1, 1100:  
Dec 1, 1099 → 31 days back to Dec 1, so from Jan 1 back 31 days → Dec 1, 1099.  
Remaining: 85 − 31 = 54 days before Dec 1, 1099.  
Nov has 30 days → back 30 days → Nov 1, 1099.  
Remaining: 54 − 30 = 24 days before Nov 1, 1099.  
Oct has 31 days → back 24 days from Nov 1 → Oct 8, 1099.  

FINAL_ANSWER: 1099-10-08
